```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import numpy as np
```

```{python}
#| echo: false

health_expenditure_wide = pd.read_csv(
    r"C:/Users/USER/Documents/GitHub/co2_emissions_demo/data/hiv-prevalance/health-expenditure/current_health_expenditure.csv",
    engine="python",  # more flexible parser
    on_bad_lines="skip",  # skips problematic rows
)

# HIV prevelence data
hiv_data = pd.read_csv(
     r"C:\Users\USER\Documents\GitHub\co2_emissions_demo\data\hiv-prevalance\health-expenditure\ddf--datapoints--estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49--by--country--year.csv",
    engine="python",
)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

# Convert column names to lowercase and remove spaces
hiv_data.columns = hiv_data.columns.str.lower().str.strip()


# Rename country column if necessary
if "country name" in hiv_data.columns:
    hiv_data = hiv_data.rename(
        columns={"country name": "country"}
    )

elif "country" not in hiv_data.columns:
    # Use the first column as country if no country column exists
    hiv_data = hiv_data.rename(
        columns={hiv_data.columns[0]: "country"}
    )


# Clean country names
hiv_data["country"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
)


# Create a readable country label
hiv_data["country_label"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .str.replace("_", " ", regex=False)
    .str.title()
)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

# Country-name differences between the HIV dataset # and the health expenditure dataset
country_map = {
    "bahamas": "Bahamas,  The",
    "cape_verde": "Cabo Verde",
    "congo_rep": "Congo,  Rep.",
    "cote_d_ivoire": "Cote d'Ivoire",
    "egypt": "Egypt,  Arab Rep.",
    "gambia": "Gambia,  The",
    "guinea_bissau": "Guinea-Bissau",
    "iran": "Iran,  Islamic Rep.",
    "lao": "Lao PDR",
    "sao_tome_and_principe": "Sao Tome and Principe",
    "south_korea": "Korea,  Rep.",
    "swaziland": "Eswatini",
    "trinidad_and_tobago": "Trinidad and Tobago",
    "turkey": "Turkiye",
    "venezuela": "Venezuela,  RB",
    "yemen": "Yemen,  Rep.",
}


# Create a World Bank-compatible country name
hiv_data["wb_name"] = (
    hiv_data["country"]
    .map(country_map)
    .fillna(hiv_data["country"].str.replace("_", " ", regex=False).str.title())
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false

# Find columns containing years
year_columns = [
    column for column in health_expenditure_wide.columns if str(column).isdigit()
]

# Convert from wide format to long format
health_expenditure_long = health_expenditure_wide.melt(
    id_vars=["Country Name", "Country Code", "Indicator Name", "Indicator Code"],
    value_vars=year_columns,
    var_name="year",
    value_name="health_expenditure",
)


# Convert year to numeric
health_expenditure_long["year"] = pd.to_numeric(
    health_expenditure_long["year"], errors="coerce"
)


# Convert health expenditure to numeric
health_expenditure_long["health_expenditure"] = pd.to_numeric(
    health_expenditure_long["health_expenditure"], errors="coerce"
)

```

```{python}
#| echo: false

hiv_data["year"] = pd.to_numeric(
    hiv_data["year"],
    errors="coerce"
)

hiv_data["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"] = pd.to_numeric(
    hiv_data["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"],
    errors="coerce"
)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

merged_data = hiv_data.merge(
    health_expenditure_long,
    left_on=["wb_name", "year"],
    right_on=["Country Name", "year"],
    how="inner"
)


# Remove missing values
merged_data = merged_data.dropna(
    subset=[
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
        "health_expenditure"
    ]
).copy()

```

# Overview 

## Project Overview 

::: {.card .intro-card}
### HIV Prevalence, Health Expenditure & ARV Treatment HIV remains an important public health and health-security concern, particularly in countries where health systems face challenges in prevention, testing, treatment, and long-term care. Adequate health financing is important for strengthening health services, including HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and access to antiretroviral (ARV) therapy. This dashboard explores HIV prevalence among people aged 15–49 and current health expenditure per capita across countries and over time. It examines HIV trends, differences in health-system investment, geographical patterns, and the relationship between HIV prevalence and health expenditure. The analysis uses Python, Pandas, NumPy, and Plotly to clean, analyse, and visualise publicly available health data. 
:::

## Why This Project Matters

::: {.card .finding-card}
The project brings together HIV prevalence and health expenditure data to identify patterns relevant to HIV prevention, testing, treatment, ARV therapy, and broader health-system strengthening. The analysis is descriptive and does not establish causal effects.

# HIV Prevalence Analysis

## Trend Over Time

```{python}
#| echo: false

hiv_trend = ( hiv_data .groupby("year", as_index=False) ["estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49"] .mean() .dropna() )
```

::: {.row height="500px"}

```{python}
#| echo: false

fig_hiv_trend = px.line(
    hiv_trend,
    x="year",
    y="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    markers=True,
    title="Average HIV Prevalence Among People Aged 15–49 Over Time",
    labels={
        "year": "Year",
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)"
    }
)

fig_hiv_trend.update_layout(
    height=500,
    xaxis_title="Year",
    yaxis_title="HIV prevalence (%)"
)

fig_hiv_trend.show()
```
:::

## Highest-Prevalence Countries

::: {.row height="600px"}

::: {.column width="40%"}

```{python}
#| echo: false

top_hiv_plot = top_hiv.sort_values(
    "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49", ascending=True
)

fig_hiv_top10 = px.bar(
    top_hiv_plot,
    x="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    y="country_label",
    orientation="h",
    title=f"Top 10 Countries by HIV Prevalence ({hiv_latest_year})",
    labels={
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)",
        "country_label": "Country",
    },
    text="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
)

fig_hiv_top10.update_traces(texttemplate="%{text:.1f}%", textposition="outside")

fig_hiv_top10.update_layout(
    height=550, yaxis_title="Country", xaxis_title="HIV prevalence (%)"
)

fig_hiv_top10.show()
```
:::
:::

::: {.card .finding-card}
**Interpretation:** HIV prevalence remains highly concentrated in Southern and Eastern Africa. The long-term pattern shows the historical development of the epidemic followed by periods of stabilization and decline, consistent with the broader context of expanded prevention and treatment efforts, including ART.
:::

# RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HIV AND HEALTH EXPENDITURE

## Relationship

```{python}
#| echo: false

# Filter data for years 2000–2011
relationship_data = merged_data[
    (merged_data["year"] >= 2000) & (merged_data["year"] <= 2011)
].copy()

# Get the latest year in the filtered data
relationship_latest_year = int(relationship_data["year"].max())

# Subset data for the latest year
relationship_latest_data = relationship_data[
    relationship_data["year"] == relationship_latest_year
].copy()
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

fig_relationship = px.scatter(
    relationship_data,
    x="health_expenditure",
    y="estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49",
    color="year",
    hover_name="country_label",
    title="HIV Prevalence vs. Health Expenditure per Capita",
    labels={
        "health_expenditure": "Health expenditure (US$ per capita)",
        "estimated_hiv_prevalence_ages_15_49": "HIV prevalence (%)",
        "year": "Year",
    },
    log_x=True,
)

fig_relationship.update_layout(height=600)

fig_relationship.show()
```


## Change Over Time


::: {.card .finding-card}
**Main finding:** The relationship between health expenditure and HIV prevalence is complex rather than simply inverse. Some countries with high HIV prevalence also have relatively high health expenditure because greater spending may reflect investment in managing a substantial HIV burden.
:::

# Conclusion 

::: {.card .conclusion-card}

## Key Findings

**1. HIV burden varies substantially.**  
HIV prevalence differs considerably between countries, with the highest levels concentrated in Southern and Eastern Africa.

**2. Health expenditure differs widely.**  
Current health expenditure per capita varies substantially across countries, reflecting differences in economic resources and health-system investment.

**3. The relationship is complex.**  
The analysis does not support a simple conclusion that higher health expenditure automatically results in lower HIV prevalence. Countries with high HIV prevalence may also have high expenditure because substantial resources are needed for prevention, testing, treatment, and ARV therapy.

**4. Sustained investment remains important.**  
Continued investment in health systems, HIV prevention, testing, treatment, ARV therapy, and health-system capacity remains important for improving long-term health outcomes.

## Limitations

This is an observational, country-level analysis. The observed relationships should therefore be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Differences in epidemic history, socioeconomic conditions, healthcare access, prevention programmes, treatment coverage, and data quality may influence the results.

:::

::: {.card .final-message}
### Final Message

**Overall, the dashboard demonstrates how publicly available health data can be combined with Python to identify patterns in HIV prevalence, health expenditure, and health-system investment. The findings highlight the importance of sustained HIV prevention, treatment, ARV therapy, and broader health-system strengthening.**
:::
